messages:
incident-bot: ALERT — service /v1/generate in us-west hitting 5xxs. Error rate crossed 6% at 09:12 UTC. Auto-paging to oncall-sre and ops on duty.

alex.k: Seeing the spike in Grafana. Affects model-serving cluster ms-gw-usw1. Paging now. Tagging enterprise accounts that saw increased errors: Aequitas Bank, CeresHealth, Triton Logistics.

samir: I’m on it — taking primary shard out of LB for health checks. Initial hypothesis: KV cache saturation + downstream redis timeouts. Starting a restart of cache pool node-3.

oncall-sre: Noted. Rolling restart started for node-3 (command: `sudo systemctl restart rcache-node.service`). Also enabling fallback routing to model-tier:stable-v2.

ops-manager: Need tailored impact lines for account emails/status page. CS teams want short, account-specific blurb we can paste. Can we get one per customer (impact + ETA + mitigation steps)?

cs-lead: Prioritize Aequitas Bank and CeresHealth (high-touch). Triton can get a slightly longer technical note. I’ll prep recipients once copy is approved.

maria: Draft status page update and customer snippets below — please review.

maria: ```Status page (short):
- Incident: Increased 5xx errors on /v1/generate (us-west)
- Impact: Some enterprise customers may see failed requests and degraded throughput
- Status: Mitigation in progress — routing to fallback model tier; caches restarting
- ETA: 15–30 minutes for full recovery; next update in 10 minutes
```

maria: Aequitas Bank customer blurb: "Aequitas Bank — We observed intermittent failures (5xx) affecting generation requests. We have rerouted traffic to a fallback model tier and restarted caching nodes. Expected resolution within 30 minutes. We will follow up with a post-incident summary and any customer-specific logs. Contact: aeq-ops@aequitas.com."

maria: CeresHealth customer blurb: "CeresHealth — Some API calls may return 5xx errors or time out. We are actively mitigating by failing over to a standby tier and warming KV caches. We expect most traffic to stabilize in 15–30 minutes. If you need immediate assistance, email ceres-support@cereshealth.com and we’ll escalate."

maria: Triton Logistics customer blurb: "Triton Logistics — Generation requests to our hosted endpoints in us-west may intermittently fail. We have triggered fallback routing and are restarting affected cache nodes. Our ops team will run a targeted verification and share logs; ETA 30–45 minutes for full verification. For account-specific escalations, use ops@tritonlogistics.com."

alex.k: Posting these to the internal cue for CS. Also adding this small routing table we used for the failover so account teams understand what we did: `route(/v1/generate)->model-tier:stable-v2 (fallback), region=us-west, weight=100`

ops-manager: Contact routing for on-call escalation (internal):
- Aequitas Bank primary: tessa.rm (aeq-amm), aeq-ops@aequitas.com
- CeresHealth primary: devin.l (ceres-eng), ceres-support@cereshealth.com
- Triton Logistics: rui.p (tlog), ops@tritonlogistics.com
Please make sure account owners are CCed when CS sends notices.

samir: Restart succeeded, cache node-3 came back healthy at 09:20 UTC. Error rate dropped from 6.2% -> 0.9%. Still seeing sporadic 503s for large prompts — keeping fallback routing until verified.

incident-bot: Deploy bot: canary rollout of model-tier:stable-v2 -> us-west initiated by samir. Canary on 5% traffic.

statusbot: Status page updated (minor) — message posted to https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/4876543210.

cs-lead: Copy approved. I’ll send tailored emails to Aequitas and Ceres now, and queue Triton with the longer note. Will attach the incident timeline and logs once we have full postmortem.

samir: Verification: error rate stabilized at 0.4% over the last 5m, latency within SLOs. Marking mitigation as effective; keeping monitoring for 1 hour before closing.

ops-manager: Thanks — after CS sends comms, schedule a 30m handoff to the post-incident review. I’ll coordinate on timeline and owner for the RCA. :white_check_mark:
